verdict.root_cause: Cart's calls into its Valkey/Redis cart store are intermittently taking ~300 ms where they normally take under 1 ms. Three traces show the cart/HGET span alone consuming ~300.6-301.2 ms with small handler self-time, while healthy traces in the same window show HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE at 0.1-0.6 ms [tr_f8e53e09966c]. Cart is otherwise normal: no deploy, config push or flag change [tr_189486765dc3], continuous info-level logs with no crash or error markers [tr_3e503166b3a3], and only intermittent mild error elevation rather than sustained failure [tr_f5d1b25eb7ad]. The downstream alerts one minute later are consistent with waiting on a slow cart; frontend-proxy's own error ratio is below its baseline [tr_fc40edd3ed73]. The mechanism is latency in the store cart depends on.
verdict.reasoning: The only localized anomaly found is inside cart's store call path, with the trace tool's degrading-hop analysis placing the bottleneck in cart's store operations and explicitly ruling out cart's own handler logic, flagd, product-catalog and network transport into cart [tr_f8e53e09966c]. Crash/restart and error-emission hypotheses are closed by logs [tr_3e503166b3a3]; catastrophic or sustained cart failure is closed by metrics [tr_f5d1b25eb7ad]; the proxy as an independent failure point is closed by its own metrics [tr_fc40edd3ed73]. With no change record [tr_189486765dc3] and no error-status spans, the symptom is a wait rather than a break, which is dependency_latency. Restart is the most direct lever to clear a stalled store connection pool; no wrong value or wrong artifact was identified to revert.
open_questions: The Valkey/Redis cart store was never dispatched - no store-side metrics, logs, eviction or connection-pool data, so store stall vs. client-side pool queuing vs. injected delay is unsettled.
The ~300 ms is suspiciously uniform across three traces, which keeps an injected or configured fixed delay plausible over organic store contention.
No latency measurement was taken on checkout, frontend or load-generator, so the propagation from cart to their 21:08:31 alerts is inferred from topology and timing, not measured.

alternatives.root_cause: A setting on cart inserts a fixed delay into its store call path, making the configured value itself the fault.
alternatives.why_not: No config push is recorded for cart [tr_189486765dc3], and even if one existed the failure is the wait in the call path, which classes as dependency_latency.

alternatives.root_cause: The Valkey cart store is itself resource-starved (memory pressure or connection saturation), slowing HGET.
alternatives.why_not: Nothing was dispatched against the store, so exhaustion is unevidenced; from cart's side the observed mechanism is only elapsed wait time [tr_f8e53e09966c].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The mechanism the evidence actually supports — ~300 ms spent inside cart's HGET span against the Valkey/Redis cart store, with small cart handler self-time and healthy store ops at 0.1–0.6 ms in the same window [tr_f8e53e09966c] — lives in a component that is not a legal target here. The cart store is not listed in the blast radius, and the two action classes that would address a store stall (restore_store, reconnect_service) are both marked UNAVAILABLE, so this system cannot perform the fix that matches the diagnosis.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention would be shown wrong if the latency is actually client-side state inside cart's own process — a wedged or exhausted connection pool — in which case recreating cart's container would clear it. The observation that would establish that, and which nobody has taken, is store-side evidence: Valkey/Redis latency, blocked-client and connection counts, plus cart's pool-wait metric. If store-side latency is clean while cart-side pool wait is ~300 ms, restart_service on cart becomes the right proposal and this abstention cost a few minutes. Conversely, if store-side latency itself shows ~300 ms, restarting cart would have changed nothing and the abstention was correct.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued degradation: cart keeps serving ~300 ms store reads, checkout/frontend/load-generator keep alerting, and the small intermittent error elevation on cart (max ~4%, [tr_f5d1b25eb7ad]) persists. The risk of the alternative — proposing restart_service on cart anyway — is larger and not symmetric: restart_service is irreversible, it discards cart's in-process state, it resets every in-flight cart request, and the evidence explicitly fails its precondition. The precondition asks that evidence point at process state; here the traces point past cart's process into a downstream store [tr_f8e53e09966c], cart's logs are continuous info-level with no crash or restart markers [tr_3e503166b3a3], and no deploy or config change exists to roll back or revert [tr_189486765dc3]. A restart that does not touch the store would recreate a healthy container, produce a visible connection reset to callers, and leave the ~300 ms HGET untouched — buying a false negative result that would wrongly push the investigation away from the store.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes, so nobody sees a change. The services already affected stay affected: cart (seed), and its callers checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, all of which alerted about a minute after cart. Note that frontend-proxy's error ratio is actually below its own baseline during this window [tr_fc40edd3ed73], so the downstream alerts are latency-shaped, not error-shaped, and will not clear until the store latency does. The recommended next step is dispatch to the Valkey/Redis cart store for store-side metrics, logs, eviction and connection-pool data — the suspiciously uniform ~300.6–301.2 ms across three traces keeps an injected or configured fixed delay at least as plausible as organic contention, and those two have different fixes.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Cart alerted first and the failure spread a minute later to checkout, frontend, proxy and the load generator — a multi-service cascade from a shared upstream, not a single quiet warning. No open incident covers it, and the cart-first ordering points upstream (flagd or cart's datastore) without enough signal to name a class.
